assamHighlights.text: The greater one-horned rhinoceros is Assam's state animal and a conservation emblem of Kaziranga and Pobitora.
The white-winged wood duck is Assam's state bird, found in forest wetlands and riverine habitats.
Kopou phul (foxtail orchid), Assam's state flower, is closely associated with Rongali Bihu.
Hollong (Dipterocarpus macrocarpus) is Assam's state tree and a characteristic evergreen-forest species.
Bihu dance is a widely recognized Assamese folk tradition, performed to seasonal music and rhythms.
Bihu is a major festival cycle; Rongali Bihu marks the Assamese New Year in spring.
O Mur Apunar Dekh — the State Song, penned by Lakshminath Bezbaroa.
“Joi Aai Axom” (“Hail Mother Assam”) is a popular expression of Assamese pride, not an official state motto.
Assamese is one of Assam's official languages; Bodo, Bengali and many Indigenous languages are also spoken across the state.
Khar is a distinctive alkaline preparation in Assamese cuisine, traditionally made with filtered plantain-ash water.
Kaji Nemu — the State Fruit, a GI-tagged lemon of Assam (declared 2024).
The Brahmaputra is a major river that shapes Assam's landscape, livelihoods and culture.

ASSAM_WORK.text: Kaziranga National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and home of the one-horned rhinoceros.
Majuli — Asia's largest river island, the heart of Sattriya culture and the sattras.
Sivasagar — the Ahom capital of six centuries.
Manas National Park — a UNESCO site for Royal Bengal tiger, golden langur and the one-horned rhino.
Guwahati — Saraighat's city, the gateway with Umananda and the Brahmaputra.
Tea gardens — Assam leads the world with the first flush and the garden family.
Silk & gamosa — the golden muga and the honour of the jaapi.
